Action: if you point me at the trail list template I'll apply the tbody or morph change there.

For the timeout length I'd use the expiry the auth server returns for the device code if there is one, and otherwise pick a sensible default and flag it for you.

Action: add a PositiveIntegerField with null=True, blank=True to the Hike model, run makemigrations, review the generated migration, and run the hikes tests.

`using` declares a resource whose `[Symbol.dispose]()` method runs automatically when the scope exits, even on return or throw, and `await using` does the same with `Symbol.asyncDispose`. Several `using` declarations in one scope are disposed in reverse order. It needs a recent TS target/lib setting, and the runtime must provide the symbols or a polyfill.
Action: I can show a small example, or check this repo's tsconfig and Node version to see if it's usable here.

The trace says something undefined has `.map` called on it at InvoiceLineItems.tsx line 24, inside InvoiceDetail. That points at an array prop or field missing for some invoices, but the paste is cut off and I haven't seen the code, so I won't claim which one.
Action: open InvoiceLineItems.tsx and InvoiceDetail, trace where that array comes from, and check what data shape reaches prod before suggesting a fix.

A prod database change is something I'd rather plan with you than apply, and I also can't see prod lag without access. I don't know yet what database setup or provider the infra uses.
Action: read the infra definitions for the prod db, draft the read replica change as a plan or PR without applying it, and ask you for read-only access to check replication lag.

There's a real difference. structuredClone keeps Dates as Dates, handles Map, Set, typed arrays and circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, empties Maps and Sets, and drops undefined. Neither copies functions, and structuredClone is available on Node 18, so you can use it.
Action: I can swap any JSON-roundtrip copies you point me at, after the current job finishes.

I'll fix recieved to received in the help text and in clients.ts, and grep for any other recieve variants. If a hit is a value other code might compare against, I'll flag it instead of changing it.
Action: grep the repo (excluding node_modules) for recieve, fix the help text and clients.ts, and list anything else I find.

Action: find where the overdue status is computed, require open status first, keep labels going through next-intl, and add tests for paid-past-due.
